beats.text: The most famous detail of the Flannan Isles mystery, where three lighthouse keepers vanished in 1900, is a logbook.
In it, the keepers record a terrible storm. One man is weeping. They are praying.
The final line reads: storm ended, sea calm, God is over all.
It is haunting. It is also fiction. Researcher Mike Dash showed the entries are not in the real station records.
And no great storm was reported in the area on the days those entries describe.
Much of the legend grew from a 1912 poem, which added a meal never eaten and an overturned chair.
The real records point somewhere simpler, and colder: the sea. Sources are in the description.
